items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: They had a sister named Camille Todd played in the sporting house.

ctx.x: And you were with him huh?

Yeah. But Doc Cook played in the same place and I worked with him at the Dream Land. Well you know Keppert played with Cook and you played with Cook too. Yeah. Is that the same place? But I thought that was Fred's band. I didn't know no band. No, I didn't know. It was Cook's. Yes it was. Old Freddy Keppert was a fine fella boy. Drank pretty good didn't he? Oh he could drink some liquor. Did you drink very much when you was younger? Yeah I did a lot of drinking. Did you? Yeah but I tell you what happened with me.…
Was this the guy from New York City? Yeah I think he was. Did you know him later in New York? I don't know.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Camilla, wasn't it? Camilla Todd Yeah, she did a little singin'

ctx.x: I see Now what about vocalists in those days? Who did they have that sang in a band? Well I'm going to tell you something Dick If you're talking about here

The musicians wasn't doing much singing in bands Now like Tuxedo they had a girl singin' Who was that? Oh the girl played the piano What name was Jeanette? No Camilla, wasn't it? Camilla Todd Yeah, she did a little singin'
And he come along though, he come along because I'll tell ya, who was it?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Well, that lady on piano, Clown's sister, Camilla Todd, is that her name?

ctx.x: Who did Celestan have in the rhythm section?

Well, that lady on piano, Clown's sister, Camilla Todd, is that her name? Mm-hmm. Now, who was on bass? Chester Zadis played bass with him, why? But before that he had George Foster, that's right. He was- He was-
He was the same one was with Jack Carey, huh? Yeah, same one.
